Agreement journal: Windows PE 53.16, offline manual decompilation
================================================================

This file and pe-manual-decompiled.c are manually reconstructed from the actual
native instructions and jump tables. They are not automatic Ghidra output and
are not game execution observations. Existing ELF output is retained separately.

Binary sources (configured data/runtime/native-pe-images.json):
  Steam: D:/program/steam/steamapps/common/Dwarf Fortress/Dwarf Fortress.exe
         PE:6a70a6d9:02711000, preferred image base 0x140000000.
  Classic: C:/Users/WIN11/Downloads/df_53_16_win/Dwarf Fortress.exe
           PE:6a70b91c:0270a000, preferred image base 0x140000000.
  pe-functions.tsv records the full source paths, identities, SHA-256 and ranges.

Complete retained source ranges, RVAs (end exclusive):
                         Steam               Classic
  Journal renderer       c2110..ca4f9         c20a0..ca489
  List/title/orders      df540..e0f67         df4d0..e0ef7
  Retained title clip    cdf30..cdfb3         cdec0..cdf43
  Calendar month leaf    773390..7734af       770db0..770ecf
  Journal card border    dec60..dee12         debf0..deda2

Original asm is saved separately for each image and role. pe-branches.tsv,
pe-conditions.tsv, pe-calls.tsv and pe-literals.tsv preserve the original
control-flow decisions, literal addresses and suppliers. pe-switches.tsv
preserves all selectors, including aliases in byte-remapped switches and the
neighboring journal tabs of the full renderer. PE unwind metadata splits some
small functions into chained chunks: clipping and border ranges include their
entire native body rather than only the first short unwind entry. The month
supplier is a leaf without an unwind entry; its decoded body ends at its ret.

Agreement panel and rendering modes
----------------------------------
  Journal tab selector 1 -> c3871, its entire card section ends before c70a4.
  Every card draws a title and its separate numeric current/total counter.
  Byte journal+278 != 0 enables expanded presentation for the selected card;
  nonselected cards then retain only their collapsed header.
  Byte journal+278 == 0 uses the compact detail forms on the listed cards.
  The expanded selected card draws subject type followed by subject prose.
  Compact JoinParty draws only Agreement concluded if end_year != -1; compact
  OfferService/RetrieveArtifact draw the shorter prose below. Other compact
  subjects have their stored titles without additional subject prose.
  Missing entry agreement or unresolved required parties omits the corresponding
  subject prose. The card title and counter have their own native source.

Retained titles and header geometry
----------------------------------
  entry+20: full list_name; entry+40: another native string; entry+60: p_list_name.
  Native cdf30 copies +20 to +60 only while p_list_name is empty, and clips +60
  to 58 bytes. PE string length is +10 and capacity +18 relative to the string.
  Journal title addst c39ba -> return c39bf receives precisely entry+60.
  Full-title recovery is justified by this exact writer and matching original
  bytes, not by assuming every title-shaped string is an agreement.
  Counter addst c3a59 -> return c3a5e is a separate numeric "current/total".
  Counter is an independent typed card source, including when a default order
  kind leaves the operation title empty but still draws its issuer and status.
  Runtime Counter recognition uses PE return c3a5e and ELF return 17cffdd, so
  those cards can be identified without inventing a missing operation title.
  Title and counter share the card's top row. The title begins left+1; counter
  begins right-length-1 and ends right-2, preserving the top right corner.
  Completed JoinParty end_year != -1 prefixes the retained title with "Done: ".

All subject types and subject-label branches
--------------------------------------------
Native renderer dispatch c3b26/table ca3e8; title constructor dfa14/table e0ed4.
The selector range is 0..17. Out-of-range default assigns no subject label.

  0 JoinParty: reason label switch listed below
  1 DemonicBinding: World Joining Agreement
  2 Residency: Residency Agreement
  3 Citizenship: Grant of Citizenship
  4 Parley: Parley Arrangement
  5 PositionCorruption: Corruption
  6 PlotStealArtifact: Artifact Theft
  7 PromisePosition: Promise of Position
  8 PlotAssassination: Assassination Plot
  9 PlotAbduct: Abduction Plot
 10 PlotSabotage: Sabotage Plot
 11 PlotConviction: data+18 corruption_action == 0 -> Foiled Bribery Conspiracy;
                    == 2 -> Foiled Corruption Conspiracy;
                    == 3 -> Foiled Embezzlement Conspiracy;
                    all other values assign no label
 12 Location: Build Structure
 13 PlotInfiltrationCoup: Infiltration Plot
 14 PlotFrameTreason: Framing Plot
 15 PlotInduceWar: War Starting Plot
 16 OfferService: Offer Service
 17 RetrieveArtifact: Retrieve Artifact

Only subjects 0, 16 and 17 emit further subject prose in this renderer. Other
subject types retain the exact subject label; no further diplomatic/intrigue
sentence may be invented for this panel.

JoinParty: all reason values, titles and expanded prose
------------------------------------------------------
Native reason switches cover 0..42, including every shared default alias:
  Type-label switch c3b89, table ca430, byte remap ca450.
  Prose switch c48d1, table ca47c, byte remap ca49c.
  Title-prefix switch dfb90, table e0f1c, byte remap e0f3c.
All nondefault reasons are exactly 0, 1, 2, 23, 24, 39 and 42. Values
3..22, 25..38, 40 and 41 alias the native default. Values outside 0..42 also
take the default. It produces no reason type/prose, but the title constructor
still appends the other participant's name after an empty prefix when the
required parties resolve. It must not translate that personal name as a label.

For each nondefault reason, fields below are independent native draw writes:

  0:
    Title: "Insurrection with " + <other participant>
    Type: Overthrow Agreement
    Prose: <member/You>, agreed to join, <party/you>,
           in insurrection against, <Group>, thereby freeing, <Site>
  1:
    Title: "Adventure with " + <other participant>
    Type: Adventuring Agreement
    Prose: <member/You>, agreed to adventure with, <party/you>,
           wherever the journey might lead
  2:
    Title: "Guided by " + <other participant>
    Type: Guide Agreement
    Prose: <member/You>, agreed to guide, <party/you>, to,
           <destination resolved by the complete fallback below>
 23:
    Title: "Rescue " + <other participant>
    Type: Rescue Agreement
    Prose: <member/You>, agreed to join, <party/you>,
           in order to be brought safely away from, <Site>
 24:
    Title: "Aid rescue with " + <other participant>
    Type: Aid Rescue Agreement
    Prose: <member/You>, agreed to join, <party/you>, in order to rescue,
           <target resolved by the HF/unit/default fallback below>
 39:
    Title: "The bound service of" + <other participant>
           (the original literal does not contain a trailing space)
    Type: Bound Servitude
    Prose: <member/You>, was bound to serve, <party/you>,
           by invocation of True Name
 42:
    Title: "Entertain people with " + <other participant>
    Type: Entertainment Agreement
    Prose: <member/You>, agreed to entertain people with, <party/you>,
           throughout the world

Party/name/default branches:
  JoinParty data+4 identifies the member party; data+8 the joined party.
  Both parties must exist, have a nonempty HF vector and resolve their first HF.
  Otherwise expanded prose is omitted. Native comparisons use the player HF id:
  the member is "You" when it matches; the joined party is "you" when it
  matches; all other participants are independent Person-name fields.
  Title uses the joined person when the member is the player, otherwise member.

Guide destination (c4e92..c507a):
  1. data+0c != -1 -> Site formatter, return site c4efd.
  2. Otherwise, data+14 resolves an HF -> Person name, return site c4fa6.
  3. Otherwise, data+10 resolves a unit via 72570 -> native unit-name resolver
     c3a4f0; a resulting name uses the Person formatter, return site c501b.
  4. Neither HF nor unit resolves -> literal somebody unknown (c506a).
  5. A unit exists but its name resolver returns null -> no destination field.
The upstream structure names the union slot +10 "entity"; this native branch
actually calls the unit lookup/name path and must be retained independently.

Aid Rescue target (c554f..c56bd):
  Same HF +14, unit +10, somebody unknown, or null unit-name branches as Guide,
  without Guide's preceding Site option. HF and unit names are Person fields at
  c55e9 and c565e; somebody unknown returns c56ad. These target blocks do not
  contain an explicit player-id comparison replacing the target with "you".

JoinParty completion and the entire date grammar
-----------------------------------------------
  Completed iff data.end_year(+18) != -1. The expanded type heading changes
  its native color, the retained title gains "Done: ", and expanded prose adds
  Agreement concluded followed by a separately drawn Date field (c5ee2).
  The expanded conclusion is reached after the resolved-party/reason block,
  including the empty default reason branch. Compact conclusion is independently
  selected by type==0 and end_year!=-1 (c6b12..c6b86), without rendering a date.
  No agreement cancellation sentence is emitted here.

  Native expanded date:
    days = end_tick / 1200; month = days / 28; day0 = days % 28;
    decimal(day0 + 1) + ordinal + " " + month_name + ", " + decimal(end_year).
  Ordinal switch c5e3e/table ca4c8/remap ca4d8 retains selectors 0..32:
    day0 0,20,30 -> st; 1,21,31 -> nd; 2,22,32 -> rd; remaining -> th.
    Values 28..32 are retained raw switch entries, even though valid day0 from
    the 28-day month arithmetic is 0..27. Out-of-range defaults to th.
  Month selector 0..11:
    Granite, Slate, Felsite, Hematite, Malachite, Galena, Limestone,
    Sandstone, Timber, Moonstone, Opal, Obsidian.
    Default returns without appending any month text. The surrounding numeric
    day/year and separators are emitted independently.

OfferService and RetrieveArtifact
---------------------------------
The renderer selects subject 16/17 after the type label. Both required parties,
their nonempty first-HF vectors and resolved figures must exist; otherwise the
corresponding prose is omitted. The player variants use You/you and other people
use Person-name fields.

  Subject 16 expanded:
    <requester/You>, requested that, <recipient/you>,
    make an offer of service to, <Group>.
  Subject 16 compact:
    <requester/You>, requested that, <recipient/you>, serve <Group>.
    "serve " and Group are separate adjacent writes on one native row.
  Subject 17 expanded:
    <requester/You>, asked that, <retriever/you>, retrieve, <Artifact>,
    optional from, <Site> when artifact_site != -1,
    optional for, <Group> when receiving_entity != -1.
  Subject 17 compact:
    <requester/You>, asked that, <retriever/you>, retrieve <Artifact>.
    "retrieve " and Artifact are separate adjacent writes on one native row;
    compact prose does not draw the Site or receiving Group fields.

All native order-kind, issuer and progress branches
-------------------------------------------------
Actual Windows PE virtual kind values are 5, 6, 7 and 8, from calls through
vtable+18 at dff2e and c42bb. They must not be relabeled as ELF order selectors.

  Kind 5:
    Constructor e0cc6: Order: Drive off <Group> from <Site>
    Expanded card c609e: Drive, <Group>, from, <Site>
  Kind 6:
    Constructor e03b4: Order: Cause trouble for <Group>
    Expanded card c5fdc: Cause trouble for, <Group>
  Kind 7:
    Constructor e017f: Order: Kill <Actor>
    Expanded card c5efb: Kill, <Actor>
  Kind 8:
    Constructor dff55: Order: Drive off <Group> from <Site>
    Expanded card c42e4: Drive members of, <Group>, out of, <Site>
  Default kind:
    No operation title/operation prose assigned; shared issuer/status remains.

  Kind 5 and 8 share the same title literals but retain distinct native
  completion and target/commander-location control flow in the constructor.
  The full native branches and decisions are saved, including missing reference
  paths. No additional English text is generated by those location decisions.
  Compact cards omit expanded operation prose but retain stored title plus the
  issuer/progress below. Missing references retain empty or native-formatted
  fields; the fixed command fragments are separate from those fields.

  Common issuer: An order from, <Actor>.
    Actor source uses native b92f10 and can format an unnamed actor reference.
  Progress branch order:
    order flags(+1c) bit 0 set -> Finish reporting in;
    otherwise entry.complete(+18) true -> Complete: report back;
    otherwise -> Not yet completed.
  Both expanded and compact forms draw the corresponding issuer/progress.
  Agreement concluded belongs to an independent concluded JoinParty entry,
  not to an order entry carrying an associated JoinParty agreement pointer.
  Selected order centering branch:
    entry.center_on_commander(+98) -> Centered on commander;
    other branch -> Centered on target.
  Shared neighboring journal location fields use Centered on location,
  Centered on first heard and Centered on last heard; they remain in the full
  renderer source but are not fabricated agreement sentences.

Agreement/order entry fields and mutually exclusive construction
--------------------------------------------------------------
  agreement_entryst fields in the actual PE layout:
    +00 ag (agreement pointer), +08 sq (squad pointer), +10 so (squad_order).
    +18 order progress bool, +20 full list_name, +40 simple_list_name,
    +60 clipped p_list_name.
  The constructor creates separate agreement and order entries:
    Agreement allocation df930 initializes +08/+10 to zero at df99d/df9a1,
    then stores the agreement pointer in +00 at df9c2.
    Order allocation dfe9c allocates 0xa8 bytes. dfe16 clears rbx before the
    order loop, dff04 stores that zero in +00, dff20 stores sq in +08 and
    dff27 stores the actual order pointer in +10. The following virtual kind
    call dff2e uses that order pointer to select the operation title.
  No order title/completion/location branch later assigns an agreement pointer
  to +00. At e0e7d rbx is cleared again before the next iteration; the default
  order-kind path reaches insertion with its original zero initialization.
  Insertion supplier cc680..cc804 only copies +20 to +40, folds that string
  to lowercase and inserts/sorts the entry pointer. It does not assign +00.
  Classic has the same constructor layout/control flow; these constructor
  instruction RVAs are Steam minus 0x70.
  Therefore a native order entry has ag==NULL, while an agreement entry has
  sq==NULL and so==NULL. Runtime title metadata can safely read the retained
  entry's +00 agreement pointer: command titles cannot acquire JoinParty
  companion metadata through this constructor. Unknown JoinParty reason names
  and the order grammar remain separate by their actual entry source.

Native typed display field sources
----------------------------------
  Steam addst is ad9960; Classic addst is ad69a0. pe-display-fields.tsv preserves
  every agreement-section addst instruction/return site with original literals.
  PE reference suppliers:
    Person a946e0; Group b92900; Site b93930; Artifact b94400; Actor b92f10;
    Date has the explicit month supplier 773390 inside the numeric date writer.
  Classic suppliers:
    Person a91760; Group b8f940; Site b90970; Artifact b91440; Actor b8ff50;
    Date month supplier 770db0.
  Title return c39bf, Type return c3ce9, Counter return c3a5e are separately
  identified by their proven native source. Classic journal returns are -70.
  Counter has its own runtime field classification and can supply card identity
  even when its title has no native operation text in the order-kind default.
  Remaining addst fields within the agreement section are Literal unless their
  exact return site identifies a typed supplier. You/you/somebody unknown are
  fixed literal branches, not guessed Person/Group/Site tokens.
  pe-typed-field-return-sites.inc lists exact Steam source-call classification
  expressions using native_reference_address for runtime address mapping.

Native card border, clipping and section ownership
-------------------------------------------------
  Frame call c3973 -> border producer dec60. Arguments:
    left=title_x-1, right=card_right, top=header_y,
    bottom=header_y+height+1, selected=(index==selected_index), alternate=false.
  Default collapsed height=-1 -> top==bottom. The expanded selected card uses
  DIMY-index-6. Titles/counters overwrite the top interior skin tiles while
  the top corners remain. The entire frame is filled by native 3x3 skin tiles;
  ownership cannot assume each tile is a generic CP437 box glyph.

  Native gfx base Steam 14264a3f0, Classic 1426442e0.
  Skin columns are contiguous triples in the order top/middle/bottom:
    Selected agreement skin +aa4c(left), +aa58(center), +aa64(right).
    Normal agreement skin   +aa70(left), +aa7c(center), +aa88(right).
    Alternate selected +aa04/+aa10/+aa1c; alternate normal +aa28/+aa34/+aa40
    are preserved border-producer branches, although this agreement caller
    passes alternate=false.
  For selected/normal cards respectively:
    NW +aa4c/+aa70; N +aa58/+aa7c; NE +aa64/+aa88;
    W  +aa50/+aa74; interior +aa5c/+aa80; E +aa68/+aa8c;
    SW +aa54/+aa78; S +aa60/+aa84; SE +aa6c/+aa90.
  Collapsed top==bottom resolves y_role=top before the bottom comparison, so
  its single row uses the top triplet cells. Expanded forms use real middle
  vertical edges and bottom corners. These native selected/normal skin values
  supply card ownership for both forms without relying on name spelling.

Runtime text handling follows the native grammar and exact field source:
fixed clauses/type headings use translation data; typed fields retain the
corresponding Person/Actor/Group/Site/Artifact formatter; stored complete titles
cover native 58-byte clipping and Done:; compact adjacent prefix/name fields
share a row without losing their original colors; default/no-text branches
preserve the absence of native text. The files here provide binary source
evidence, not evidence of observed game-screen results.
